subject: Culture
title: Why We Ritualize Death
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why We Ritualize Death usable.

hook.text: Elephants return to the bones of their dead and touch them gently with their trunks. Even animals mourn.

buildup.text: The earliest known burial is 100,000 years old—a child placed carefully in a cave with seashell offerings.

discovery.text: Anthropologist Ernest Becker argued that all culture is a defense against death anxiety. Ritual manages terror.

twist.text: Cultures without death rituals don't exist. No society simply disposes of bodies without ceremony.

climax.text: Death rituals don't help the dead. They help the living process loss and rebuild social structure.

punchline.text: Funerals are for the survivors, not the departed.

quiz.question: Who argued that all culture is a defense against death anxiety?
